visual_format: drawn illustration: non-graphic line diagram comparison, 2 slides
visual_text: A sheath collects urine without a tube in the bladder
For men who can empty their bladder but need urine collected
Indwelling catheter: a tube that stays in the bladder
Sheath: worn outside the body over the penis
Saint, J Am Geriatr Soc, 2006; Gould, CDC guideline, 2010
Trial of 75 hospital men, average age about 73
More men said it was comfortable. Combined measure mostly bacteria in urine tests.

Men with a sheath were more likely to say it was comfortable and not painful. The combined measure was mostly bacteria in the urine on daily testing, and was lower with the sheath only after adjustment. In men with dementia the trial did not show a clear difference.
Only for men who can pass urine on their own
Saint, J Am Geriatr Soc, 2006; Hamilton, Br J Community Nurs, 2026
alt_text: Two line diagrams of the lower body from the side. Left, indwelling catheter: a tube runs from the bladder out to a drainage bag at the thigh. Right, sheath: worn outside over the penis with a short tube to a drainage bag, nothing inside the bladder. For men who can empty their bladder but need urine collected.

Trial of 75 hospital men, average age about 73. Men with a sheath were more likely to say it was comfortable and not painful. The combined measure was mostly bacteria in urine on daily testing, lower with the sheath only after adjustment. No clear difference in dementia. Checklist of five points for a sheath.
